paragraphs_over6.paragraph: Financial path-risk studies document that a within-period extreme can matter more than the value observed at the end of the period. MaxVaR evaluates the worst cumulative portfolio return under a fixed portfolio and diffusion assumptions, including a conversion from endpoint probabilities to path risk (Boudoukh et al.(2004)) . The payment-liquidity thesis constructs a conditional quantile buffer for the maximum cumulative negative payment balance using transaction-path simulation and extreme-value tail estimation (van den Hoogen(2017)) . Its one-sided cash deficit differs from sampled absolute inventory, and its confidential records and complete engine remain outside our executed comparisons. Related settlement studies examine tail liquidity needs and collateral requirements in their respective payment systems (Petrunia et al.(2019); Arjani et al.(2020)) . Duffie and colleagues analyze dealer capacity and Treasury-market functioning, with additional out-of-sample PnL quantile comparisons in their appendix (Duffie et al.(2023)) . Our empirical contribution concerns matched forecasts of the present peak-position target across the FX record and related public position aggregates.

The new simulation grid satisfies its prespecified short-history and long-history prediction screens across the pooled cases and reported method and process subgroups. The short-history criterion is met in 47 of 48 applicable cells, while the applicable regions remain fixed from each method's discovery cutpoint. The long-history criterion is met in 21 of 24 applicable cells, supporting the loss pattern for these procedures under the new innovation laws. The universal simplification criterion holds in 42 of 48 paired cells, so its all-cell prediction fails and the counterexamples remain part of the finding. The Supplement reports complete screen denominators and universal-simplification failures. Its linked technical tables display every primary-screen exception, while indexed public archives retain candidate and repetition records. Shared simulation streams make these cell counts dependent summaries, so passing the screen supplies procedure-specific evidence rather than a population significance test.

The later analyses and working-reference tests describe the observed records after earlier results had informed the research process and additional comparisons. Their p-values therefore do not account for the full sequence of model, sample, diagnostic, and presentation choices made during that process. Filtered-path, quantile-forest and headroom-SAV comparisons evaluate finite, resource-bounded specifications rather than entire method classes. Numerical or structural failures remain unavailable comparisons; these executions neither inherit source-method guarantees nor evaluate SPCI or simultaneous-trajectory calibration. The finite calibration wrapper, empirical endpoint rule, and dependent financial paths also require distinctions from the population assumptions in Proposition . The main evidence supports a bounded comparative forecasting result, with external validity, prospective calibration, and economic decision value remaining questions for future evaluation. The score uses a nineteen-to-one error-weight ratio for evaluation, which does not measure the actual costs of a limit decision.

writing.abstract_text: Peak-position limits concern the largest absolute inventory reached before a review ends, making completed path labels and the observed current position central to forecasting. We compare historical and conditional quantile reports for an FX market maker and weekly primary-dealer position aggregates, using matched histories and update schedules. Simple historical rules remain demanding benchmarks across frequencies, position categories and reference choices. At the shorter horizon, long-history FX regression lowers matched loss by 14.8% and 16.6% in the previously reported later and earlier windows. A post hoc history-to-horizon coordinate organizes simulation gains, and a new simulation passes its short-history and long-history prediction screens. Real-record learning curves partly support the predicted first cutpoints, while left censoring, large-history reversals and failures of universal simplification qualify that pattern. For limit managers, these findings motivate matching historical information before assessing conditional forecasts jointly on score, breaches and stability, with history length guiding evaluation.
